evidence.quote: X Lab X-ray Laboratory for Research on Quantum Materials Welcome! Welcome to the Frano X Lab (a.k.a The X-ray Laboratory for Research on Quantum Materials). Based at the University of California, San Diego near the sunny beaches of La Jolla, CA, our group studies the fascinating properties of materials with strongly correlated electrons. We are interested in investigating long-range periodicities in the spin, charge, and orbital quantum states observed in transition-metal-oxide films, superlattices, heterostructures and single crystals. To explore these spatially periodic behaviors we operate in Fourier space by performing modern x-ray scattering experiments at synchrotrons around the world. Feel free to explore our website for more information. News We discovered an anisotropic spin-liquid-like state emerging from disorder in a Kitaev magnet, reported in npj Quantum Materials (2026). Our discovery that thin films can “push and pull” on their substrates was highlighted in UC San Diego Today . Our work on VO 2 neuromorphic devices was recognized as a finalist for the 2026 ACS Nano Impact Award (2026). We expand our research horizons from hard condensed matter to soft matter, using neutron scattering to probe the dynamics of polymer-integrated protein crystals . Publications Publication highlights: We harnessed a nickelate phase transition to enhance spin-to-charge conversion (2026). We Discovered That Switching Thin Films Imprint Strain Deep Into Their Substrates (2026). We Explored How Operando Microscopy Can Guide the Future of Neuromorphic Hardware (2026).
